sets.title: CSV row parser with local variables renamed
sets.description: The same CSV row-parsing method in three importer classes. Carrier A is pristine; carrier B renames one local variable; carrier C renames every local variable consistently. Structure and layout are byte-identical — only identifiers differ (Type-2), so identifier-canonicalizing token tools, AST, metric and semantic detectors should still match all three.
sets.notes: Only local variables are renamed (RN-01); parameters, calls, literals and layout are untouched, so the single axis is identifier renaming. Pristine (A) vs fully-renamed (C) is the discriminating pair.

distractors.reason: near-miss: same CSV vocabulary and foreach-over-columns shape, but builds a column-width histogram — a different result

sets.title: CSV row parser with one local variable renamed and used 6 times
sets.description: G-5 gap-fill: One variable renamed but used 6 times throughout the method. The same CSV row-parsing method in three importer classes. Carrier A is pristine; carrier B renames one variable that appears 6 times in the method; carrier C renames all variables consistently. This tests whether detectors can match when a single高频变量 is renamed across multiple usages — a more realistic rename scenario than a once-used variable.
sets.notes: G-5 gap-fill: rung-2 micro-step 'one variable renamed, used 6 times'. This is between 'renamed once-used var' and 'all locals renamed'. The高频 variable rename is more challenging for text-based detectors.
